issues.title: b4w wrapper argument passing broken in bash/Linux environment

sections.body: ./b4w.ps1 goto "https://www.amazon.com" or ./b4w.sh goto "https://www.amazon.com" from bash
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Arguments 'goto' and 'https://www.amazon.com' should pass through to the browser4-cli binary.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The TopHelp text from b4w.ps1 is emitted, followed by the browser4-cli help text and 'Unknown command: —'. The binary never receives the correct arguments. The cargo output shows the entire help text being passed as arguments to the binary instead of 'goto' and the URL.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The b4w.sh script uses `exec pwsh -Command "& '$SCRIPT_DIR/b4w.ps1' $ARGS"` where $ARGS is individually quoted. The exec within a command substitution $(...) appears to cause argument corruption. Additionally, the b4w.ps1 script's $TopHelp heredoc contains em-dash characters ('—') that may trigger PowerShell string interpolation issues when combined with Invoke-Expression on line 478.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: b4w.sh lines 34-51 and b4w.ps1 lines 470-488
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Add a direct bash-native launcher (e.g. b4w binary wrapper) that doesn't require PowerShell as an intermediary on Linux
- Fix b4w.sh to not use exec inside command substitution contexts
- Replace Invoke-Expression in b4w.ps1 line 478 with a direct call operator invocation (e.g. & $Exe @CliArgs) to avoid string interpolation issues with special characters
- Add a cargo alias or Makefile target so users on Linux can run `make run -- goto <url>` without wrestling with shell wrappers
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: DEFAULT session spontaneously reverts to previous page (Wikipedia)

sections.body: 1. Have a pre-existing DEFAULT session on Wikipedia. 2. goto to Amazon. 3. Wait or run several commands. 4. The browser silently returns to Wikipedia.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: After goto navigates to Amazon, the session should stay on Amazon until explicitly navigated elsewhere.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: After successful goto to Amazon (confirmed by the CLI output showing 'Navigated to https://www.amazon.com'), subsequent commands (eval, htmlsnapshot) execute on Wikipedia instead. This happened 3+ times during the session. The page URL confirmed via eval showed 'https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language)'.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Possible causes: (a) the backend's session reconnection logic restores the original session URL on reconnection; (b) a race condition where the navigation completes but the CDP connection drops, and on reconnect the backend loads the last-known URL from session state; (c) a browser extension or service worker in the pre-existing session triggers navigation back. Investigation needed: check PulsarWebDriver session reconnection logic and whether goto properly updates the backend's session URL state before the CDP page load event fires.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: browser4-core/browser4-browser/ — PulsarWebDriver session management and reconnection logic
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Ensure goto atomically updates the session's canonical URL in the backend before the CDP navigation completes
- Add a post-navigation verification step that checks the actual page URL matches the requested URL
- Log a warning if the page URL changes unexpectedly between commands
- Document that pre-existing sessions may have stale state and recommend using fresh named sessions (-s <name>) for reliable automation
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: htmlsnapshot inspect returns content from wrong page

sections.body: 1. goto to Amazon search results. 2. htmlsnapshot capture (shows Amazon URL). 3. htmlsnapshot inspect 'div[data-component-type]'
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Inspect should analyze the most recently captured Amazon HTML snapshot.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Inspect returned Wikipedia infobox data (tr, th.infobox-label, #mwDA) even though the capture step showed 'Snapshot: Amazon.com : Calabi-Yau'. The get command with a product-specific selector DID return Amazon data, suggesting inspect and get may read from different snapshot storage or the inspect command searches across all stored snapshots.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Likely a storage isolation issue: htmlsnapshot commands may not properly scope to the most recent capture, or the inspect command searches a different snapshot index than get/query. The 'div[data-component-type]' selector may match elements in a previously stored Wikipedia snapshot that takes precedence in the inspection index.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- htmlsnapshot inspect should operate exclusively on the most recently captured snapshot
- Add a --session or --snapshot-id flag to explicitly target a specific snapshot
- Display which snapshot is being inspected in the output header
- Add a warning if inspect finds matches in a snapshot other than the most recent one
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: htmlsnapshot get attr returns empty array for valid selectors

sections.body: After capturing an Amazon search results snapshot: htmlsnapshot get all attr 'a.a-link-normal.s-line-clamp-2' href
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Should return an array of href URLs from matching product title links.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Returned empty array [], even though the same selector with 'get all text' successfully returned product titles.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Possible mismatch between the DOM query used for text extraction (which uses textContent) vs attribute extraction (which may use a different traversal or query method). The href attributes may be stored on parent <a> elements while the text selector matches a child <span>, causing the attribute lookup to fail.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Document the selector-to-attribute mapping behavior clearly
- Add an example showing how to extract href from link elements
- Consider relaxing the element matching for attr extraction to climb to the nearest parent with the requested attribute
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Price extraction via htmlsnapshot get returns empty for Amazon price selectors

sections.body: htmlsnapshot get all text 'a.a-link-normal.s-no-hover' on an Amazon search results page snapshot
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Should return price text values.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Returned empty array []. The elements exist in the DOM (visible in the htmlsnapshot interactive elements list) but the get command does not match them.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The stored HTML snapshot may strip or transform certain elements that contain prices (e.g., spans within links that use aria labels or dynamic content). Amazon prices are often rendered via JavaScript or use complex nested structures that don't survive the static HTML capture process.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Document which types of page content survive htmlsnapshot capture vs which require eval
- Add a note in the interactive elements output indicating which elements' text may not be extractable via get
- Consider adding JavaScript-rendered content capture to htmlsnapshot
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: No built-in e-commerce product extraction recipe or template

sections.body: Attempt to extract structured product data (title, price, rating, URL) from Amazon search results using only documented workflows.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: A documented recipe, template, or built-in command for extracting product listings from common e-commerce sites.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The htmlsnapshot-scenarios.md reference is mentioned in SKILL.md but contains patterns that don't work on the current Amazon DOM. Users must discover Amazon's actual DOM structure via eval, which requires JavaScript knowledge. The inspect command's auto-discovery didn't surface product card selectors.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: E-commerce sites frequently change their HTML structure. The documented scenarios may target older versions of Amazon's markup. The inspect auto-discovery algorithm appears to prioritize the largest container (entire page) over mid-level repeating patterns (product cards).
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Add an 'amazon' or 'ecommerce' subcommand that auto-detects and extracts product listings from major retailers
- Improve inspect auto-discovery to prefer mid-level repeating containers (e.g., same-class siblings with similar child structure) over page-level containers
- Add an 'eval --extract-products' built-in that bundles common e-commerce extraction scripts
- Ship updated e-commerce scenario files that match current Amazon/Walmart/eBay DOM structures
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: Shell quoting for eval causes friction on Linux

sections.body: cargo run ... -- eval "JSON.stringify({url: location.href})" — nested quotes require escaping
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: Simple eval expressions should work without quote-escaping gymnastics.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: Nested quotes in eval expressions require careful escaping (e.g., escaping single quotes within the JSON string). The --file option mitigates this, but requires an extra step of writing a JS file first.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: Shell quote processing combined with cargo run's argument passing creates multiple levels of quote interpretation. The SKILL.md warns about this for Windows but it affects Linux too.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body:
- Add 'eval --json' flag that automatically JSON-stringifies the result, removing the need for manual JSON.stringify wrapping
- Support eval --stdin for piping JS directly
- Document the --file pattern as the recommended approach for all platforms, not just Windows
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement

issues.title: b4w wrapper emits extraneous warning about short flags when none are used

sections.body: Run any b4w command — the warning 'Short flags detected: -i, -i' appears even when -i is not in the user's command.
sections.label: Reproduction

sections.body: The short flag warning should only appear when short flags are actually used.
sections.label: Expected Behavior

sections.body: The warning always appears because the b4w.ps1 script's $COMMON_INTERCEPTED check triggers on -i flags that appear in the script's own internal processing or cargo output, not just user-provided arguments.
sections.label: Actual Behavior

sections.body: The $COMMON_INTERCEPTED check on line 39-41 of b4w.ps1 scans $RemainingArgs which includes tokens from cargo output or internal argument processing, not just user-provided CLI arguments.
sections.label: Root Cause Analysis

sections.body: b4w.ps1 lines 39-46
sections.label: Code Pointer

sections.body:
- Move the check to only scan arguments before they're passed to cargo/build steps
- Or suppress the warning when the flags originate from internal tooling rather than user input
sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
